open_obligations: Check whether the question-distribution part of the limitation is addressed.
Check that RL beating BC holds on full-book evaluation, not only on subtasks.
Check whether Wu et al.'s RL policies maximize a learned reward function, and if so whether it is learned from human comparisons at each node or from whole-book judgements.
in.other_title: RL beats behavioral cloning at 175B; first-subtree training generalizes to full tree
in.rationale: Christiano et al. note that in their experiments X is trained by supervised learning from Amplify_H(X), whereas in many important applications they suspect they would learn a reward function from Amplify_H(X) and train X to maximize it. Wu et al. report that their 175B RL policies significantly outperform their 175B BC baseline, though the improvement is smaller for the 6B models.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether recursive decomposition can be trained with learned rewards and RL rather than supervised learning, for book summarisation

text: The authors note X is trained by supervised learning from Amplify_H(X), whereas many important applications would likely learn a reward function from it and train X with RL. They also state the question distribution D must be broad enough to cover all subquestions asked during amplification, and that in the experiments D was usable directly whereas realistically the designer would have to construct it.
title: Question distribution must cover all subquestions; supervised rather than reward learning
